title: Emergency AI scientist: 10-week delivery plan

tasks.name: Lock the two contributions and all required outputs
tasks.acceptance: Askar reviews one primary forecasting claim, one applied emergency-scientist validation, and the seven mandatory SynX outputs; no promise of publication acceptance.

tasks.name: Request access, lab slot and publication permissions
tasks.acceptance: Named SynX experimental owner; Portal/API, paired data, residue assets, compute and Tinker access requests recorded; availability is not assumed.

tasks.name: Audit pilot evidence and establish reproducible run ledger
tasks.acceptance: Check actual scheduler/output evidence; separate existing CPU pilot results from queued/unverified GPU runs; commit hashes, seeds, data versions and costs recorded.

tasks.name: Urgent: confirm lab route, lead times and data return
tasks.acceptance: SynX confirms a feasible library/reagent preparation route, one selection round by W7, and usable readout by W8D3. If unavailable, mark mandatory lab deliverable at risk immediately.

tasks.name: Select live Tinker models and cap total spend
tasks.acceptance: Query actual trainable capabilities; freeze three supported open-weight model IDs/configurations, LoRA settings and renderer modes, or explicitly narrow generalization claims. Record an approved spend ceiling and throughput estimate.
tasks.note: Local Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 is a pilot comparator, not an assumed Tinker base; current docs list it as retired.

tasks.name: W4 feasibility and novelty review after catch-up
tasks.acceptance: Confirm lab slot, data rights, scorer validity, trainable models, and a distinguishable forecasting question. Record unresolved blockers with owner and deadline.

tasks.name: Choose the platform improvement from measured failures
tasks.acceptance: Select one bounded improvement with a failing baseline, implementation estimate and independent validation metric; retain residue/rotamer limitations as measured hypotheses.

tasks.name: Freeze SynX scientific scope and London readiness
tasks.acceptance: Both family dossiers, historical replay, improvement evaluation, prospective prediction file and safety benchmark manifest are complete; London agenda accepted; no new feature scope.

tasks.name: Authorize the measured training/evaluation matrix
tasks.acceptance: Measured API throughput and token counts fit the spend ceiling and W9D3 finish; inference protocol and forecast train/test groups frozen before seeing high-budget results.

tasks.name: Freeze results and final claims
tasks.acceptance: Each figure traces to an immutable run manifest; negative results retained; missing required outputs explicitly flagged; paper and presentation use the same claims.

tasks.name: Specify emergency episodes and decision rubric
tasks.acceptance: Specify timestamps, hidden outcomes, evidence state, tool permissions, action budget, readiness rubric and failure categories; reviewers can score a toy episode consistently.

tasks.name: Freeze public data provenance and split policy
tasks.acceptance: ProteinGym GB1 and ATLAS remain component pilots; historical/public evidence collections are source-versioned; split by parent/backbone, target/family or study as appropriate.

tasks.name: Build small development episode set and baselines
tasks.acceptance: Twelve proposed development episodes span incomplete evidence, contradictions, deadlines and missing tools; fixed rubric, scripted workflow and single-response retrieval baselines run with matched access.
tasks.note: Twelve is a planning target, not an existing dataset count; freeze final sample size after the audit.

tasks.name: Implement evidence state and resource-accounted tools
tasks.acceptance: Every retrieval/structure/design action updates cited evidence, uncertainty and actual token/tool/wall-time cost; invalid actions are logged and charged.

tasks.name: Run emergency stress and public-pilot comparisons
tasks.acceptance: Compare complete versus degraded evidence and immediate versus delayed feedback; report quality/cost fronts and failure cases; GB1/ATLAS conclusions stay within their measured endpoints.

tasks.name: Build adaptive action policy v1
tasks.acceptance: Policy can request evidence, rerank, allocate a calculation and stop with uncertainty; all four actions complete an end-to-end development replay.
tasks.note: Extends the dossier policy in COSCI-13 over the six-action space; it is not a new general-purpose scientist framework. The deterministic baselines already pass the stability metric by construction, so this task is judged on whether the LLM policy holds the recommendation under irrelevant evidence at matched cost.

tasks.name: Curate two prototype-family evidence packets
tasks.acceptance: Two distinct families chosen with Askar/SynX; each has sourced essentiality, accessibility, conservation, tractability, uncertainty and a held-out episode. Selection criteria documented.
tasks.evidence: data/processed/targets/{coronaviridae,orthomyxoviridae,henipavirus}.json: 11 targets across 3 families, 59 sourced evidence entries against the seven-axis rubric, 8 update probes, 3 claims flagged as needing a citation. Awaiting the family decision with Askar and SynX.

tasks.name: Assemble time-stamped COVID historical replay
tasks.acceptance: January-March 2020 retrieval cutoffs verified; checkpoint decisions scored against information available then; pretrained hindsight limitations explicitly retained.

tasks.name: Calibrate expert scoring and freeze held-out rubric
tasks.acceptance: At least two reviewers score a calibration subset; disagreements and score definitions resolved on development outputs; held-out labels remain sealed.

tasks.name: Integrate policy with frozen molecular tools
tasks.acceptance: Both family episodes pass intake → evidence → target ranking → design recommendation; policy comparisons share tool/model versions.

tasks.name: Run held-out decisions, family transfer and ablations
tasks.acceptance: All four baselines evaluated on historical and two-family held-out episodes; ablate adaptation and evidence state; report quality, evidence support, latency, cost and reviewer uncertainty.

tasks.name: Freeze the emergency scientist demo and findings
tasks.acceptance: A recorded replay and offline fallback work; no antiviral efficacy claim without an assay; central plots and errors are ready before London.

tasks.name: Specify the target dossier decision state and action space
tasks.acceptance: Decision state is the seven-axis dossier with per-axis citations, timestamps and open uncertainties; action space is retrieve evidence, request structure, rerank, invoke design tool, recommend experiment, stop. Evidence dated after the decision clock is refused and the refusal is recorded. Hard-gate axes block a ranking.
tasks.note: Named targets reintroduce pretrained-hindsight risk that the date boundary does not control; it needs a separate audit in COSCI-08.
tasks.evidence: hpc_pilots/dossier.py with four isolation tests; date-boundary and conflict-retention tests pass.

tasks.name: Build pathogen decision environments and the subtype transfer split
tasks.acceptance: Mpro, HA H1 and HA H3 staged from the ProteinGym archive as disjoint-pool decision environments with per-landscape assay endpoints recorded; pool geometry shrinks rather than reusing candidates across pools described as disjoint; H1-to-H3 is a grouped study-and-subtype holdout.
tasks.evidence: 10 pools for Mpro, 19 for HA H1, 20 for HA H3; 240 paired replays recorded under runs/targets/.

tasks.name: Score evidence-update stability in emergency episodes
tasks.acceptance: Episodes release relevant, contradictory and irrelevant evidence at timed checkpoints under a deadline and an action budget; the policy is scored on updating when relevant evidence arrives, holding the recommendation when irrelevant evidence arrives, and retaining contradictory evidence beside the claim it contests.
tasks.note: Deterministic baselines are stable by construction; the metric earns its value on the LLM policy in COSCI-06.
tasks.evidence: Six episodes across three families; deterministic baselines hold the recommendation but reorder the tail, and the scripted workflow misses the deadline.

tasks.name: Audit residue registry, scores and experimental endpoints
tasks.acceptance: Identity/stereochemistry/codon mapping, scorefunction, rotamer assets, parent groups, assay endpoints, replicates, missingness and censoring audited; usable campaign tables identified.
tasks.note: Blocked until the campaign export arrives. It blocks MOL-02, MOL-03 and therefore MOL-04, the mandatory platform improvement. The building-block registry in MOL-08 holds the schema this export fills.

tasks.name: Measure molecular ranking and representation failures
tasks.acceptance: Rosetta ranking and simple chemistry/similarity/supervised baselines use grouped splits; inspect motif/backbone/campaign confounding and unsupported residue representations.

tasks.name: Freeze design/refolding/filter contracts
tasks.acceptance: RFdiffusion/BoltzGen version and actual chemistry support documented; refolding and geometric filters are separate logged stages; generation outputs are compatible with the permitted SynX route.

tasks.name: Implement one justified SynX platform improvement
tasks.acceptance: Fix the selected observed failure, such as residue validation or uncertainty-aware campaign ranking; run affected failing examples and a clean unaffected control set.

tasks.name: Evaluate improvement and low-label ranking module
tasks.acceptance: Before/after evaluated with independent endpoint and matched costs; zero/few-shot label budgets and grouped transfer are reported if paired data support them; newly uploaded proposal incorporated before freezing.
tasks.note: No separate few-shot proposal is currently reviewed. This schedule reserves integration time; an unsupported module cannot substitute for the required platform improvement.

tasks.name: Finalize both family target dossiers and library proposal
tasks.acceptance: Both families include evidence-backed target/epitope ranks; selected non-canonical macrocyclic library is compatible with SynX display constraints and independently reviewed.
tasks.note: Requires SynX design staff to prepare/review the compatible library; the estimate is William’s review/integration time, not full design-team effort.

tasks.name: Freeze prospective candidate ranks and analysis plan
tasks.acceptance: Immutable candidates/ranks, controls, intended measured endpoints and analysis rules recorded before laboratory outcomes; retain all submitted candidates and failures.

tasks.name: Represent non-canonical blocks and read out enrichment
tasks.acceptance: Building-block registry covers canonical and non-canonical classes with initiator and closure roles and every platform-supplied field explicitly pending; the encoding extends past the canonical twenty; acquisition metrics report an enrichment ratio against the pool baseline alongside the per-candidate view.
tasks.note: Chemical identifiers, codons, Rosetta parameters and rotamer libraries stay null until the MOL-01 export arrives. No measured macrocycle outcome exists yet, so no enrichment figure here is a macrocycle result.
tasks.evidence: 29 blocks, 9 non-canonical; enrichment ratio added to every binding and target checkpoint; the recorded GB1 replays still reproduce bit-identically.

tasks.name: Agree the single-round experimental question
tasks.acceptance: SynX confirms the designed library, feasible target/assay endpoint, controls, replicates, primary readout and what one round can substantiate; no invented affinity/antiviral endpoint.
tasks.note: Re-pointed from MOL-01 to COSCI-07 on October 19: the experimental question is answerable from the dossier and does not need the campaign export. Still gated on GATE-04, the named experimental owner.

tasks.name: SynX prepares reagents, library and booked slot
tasks.acceptance: SynX staff report validated inputs, shipping/reagent/library lead times and a reserved W7 selection slot; William's effort is coordination only.
tasks.note: SynX can prepare available inputs after the route gate while the final question/designs are refined; preparation must finish by W6D5. This overlap requires the experimental lead’s confirmation.

tasks.name: Review design-to-display compatibility
tasks.acceptance: Experimental lead signs off library representation, chemical alphabet, input format and endpoint; any incompatible designs revised before prediction freeze.

tasks.name: Prepare London dossier and book review agenda
tasks.acceptance: Send-ready pack includes two-family dossiers, model limitations, platform before/after, frozen prospective predictions, assay questions and W8 data-handoff checklist.

tasks.name: London travel and arrival
tasks.acceptance: Travel day protected from coding or critical job launches; actual itinerary to replace project-day placeholder.
tasks.note: W7D1 travel placement is proposed; the visit week is fixed, specific travel dates are not.

tasks.name: London: facility tour and design/experiment review
tasks.acceptance: Walk through portal-to-wet-lab handoff with SynX; reconcile predicted versus actual constraints; obtain expert review of both dossiers and the frozen experiment plan.

tasks.name: London: observe the required display round
tasks.acceptance: SynX executes one actual mRNA display selection round against the designed library; record performed date, inputs, controls, failures and sample provenance. Visit alone does not meet this requirement.
tasks.note: Exact execution day and duration must be confirmed at GATE-04; the Gantt window is not evidence of booking.

tasks.name: London: review discrepancies and secure data handoff
tasks.acceptance: Review unexplained score/measurement differences and platform patch; agree raw and processed readout format, QC metadata, owner and delivery by W8D3.

tasks.name: Return travel and archive the London review
tasks.acceptance: Capture accepted changes and experimental limitations; return travel protected; no major new architecture work.

tasks.name: SynX processes and returns selection-round readout
tasks.acceptance: Receive analysable readout and sample/control metadata by W8D3; QC failures stay in the report. SynX confirms actual processing/sequence turnaround before the slot.
tasks.note: If readout is late, experimental obligation stays incomplete and takes protected buffer; it is not relabeled optional.

tasks.name: Analyze the round and update the decision state
tasks.acceptance: Compare preregistered ranks with the measured endpoint, quantify uncertainty at independent units, include controls/failures and show how evidence changes the recommendation.

tasks.name: Translate grant into benign task/loss specification
tasks.acceptance: Define conclusion accuracy, evidence grounding and process validity separately; scalar normalization/weights and threat-claim boundary documented; supervised biology reasoning is benign.

tasks.name: Select public transcriptomic collections and worlds
tasks.acceptance: Audit scPerturb NormanWeissman2019 (GSE133344), DixitRegev2016 (GSE90063), and ReplogleWeissman2022; confirm versions, perturbation/metadata availability, licenses and annotation quality before using them. Pin a CELLxGENE LTS build for background/reference packets only.
tasks.note: Public atlas candidates are starting points; observational annotations are not automatic causal ground truth.

tasks.name: Specify train/test boundaries and counterfactual mechanisms
tasks.acceptance: Split by study/donor/mechanism family, never random cells; paired synthetic worlds share observable correlations while latent mechanisms differ; inference and training budgets are separate fields.

tasks.name: Build and validate small synthetic world generator
tasks.acceptance: Oracle recovers known latent answers; evidence disclosure and confounding/corruption/shift/horizon knobs verified on development worlds; held-out mechanisms remain sealed.

tasks.name: Prepare real-study task packets and expert references
tasks.acceptance: At least three audited studies proposed for generalization; references distinguish measured perturbation evidence from expert interpretation; metadata leakage and donor overlap checked.

tasks.name: Freeze tool primitives, signatures and budget accounting
tasks.acceptance: Same tool outputs/quality across checkpoints; five conditions: clean, confounding, mechanism shift, evidence corruption and longer horizon. Fixed inference budget and decomposed losses survive toy replays.

tasks.name: Measure zero-shot stress signatures on chosen bases
tasks.acceptance: Run all three exact Tinker base configurations on sealed evaluation packets at the fixed inference budget; pair case/rollout seeds, include errors and costs; no post-training outcomes used.

tasks.name: Freeze task worlds, curricula and forecast protocol
tasks.acceptance: Benign reasoning-only and evidence/tool/planning curricula are frozen; case sets, loss weights, low-budget inputs, high-budget targets and grouped forecast folds registered before London.

tasks.name: London: expert-audit safety task realism
tasks.acceptance: Discuss biological plausibility and label uncertainty; any changed test item is versioned and removed from preexisting locked comparison, or all matched baselines rerun.

tasks.name: Early Tinker access and minimal checkpoint smoke
tasks.acceptance: One tiny benign toy training/save/resume/sample path works within agreed spend; distinguish optimizer-state and sampler checkpoints; no research sweep launched.
tasks.note: This is risk retirement before London; the main harness build remains W8-W10.

tasks.name: W8D1: implement train/eval adapters and event schema
tasks.acceptance: Shared evaluator accepts exact base or adapter checkpoint; records training tokens, inference tokens, tool calls, run IDs, failures and cost without changing tool quality.

tasks.name: W8D2: checkpoint resume, sampling and idempotent jobs
tasks.acceptance: Interrupt/restart a toy run without token double counting; sampler weights reproduce a stored evaluation; optimizer resume and evaluation artifacts have separate paths.

tasks.name: W8D3: validate scorer and baseline parity
tasks.acceptance: Reproduce frozen zero-shot cases within registered sampling variation; no hidden labels enter prompts; budget exhaustion and corrupted evidence yield valid scored failures.

tasks.name: W8D3-4: pilot low-budget curves and measure throughput
tasks.acceptance: One curriculum/model reaches b and 4b cumulative training tokens; observed throughput estimates the full matrix, failure/retry overhead and sampling cost.

tasks.name: W8D4-5: launch low-budget cohort
tasks.acceptance: Twelve proposed trajectories (3 models × 2 curricula × 2 training seeds) reach b and 4b; nested curricula and fixed inference settings; forecast inputs locked before high-budget scoring.
tasks.note: Wall-clock completion is conditional on measured service capacity; primary matrix is authorized at GATE-09.

tasks.name: W8D5: produce development-only high-budget targets
tasks.acceptance: Extend the eight trajectories from two preregistered development models to 16b/64b; expose only development-case outcomes to forecaster fitting. Third-model high-budget outcomes remain sealed.
tasks.note: These are eight of the twelve curves, not extra training curves. GATE-09 must verify they can finish by W8D5; otherwise the prospective forecast date moves before the held-out result reveal.

tasks.name: W9D1-3: complete 16b/64b training and evaluation
tasks.acceptance: Finish the four held-out-model trajectories and sealed evaluations of all twelve curves; cumulative b/4b/16b/64b checkpoints and matched inference settings. Keep high-budget held-out targets unread until FCAST-02 predictions are saved.

tasks.name: W9D3: inference-budget control and tool-quality audit
tasks.acceptance: A preregistered subset repeats at a second inference budget; ensure reported training uplift is not an inference-budget or tool-output change.

tasks.name: W10D1: reproduce principal curves from clean checkout
tasks.acceptance: A clean checkout loads frozen artifacts and reproduces all principal tables/figures; limited sampler spot checks only, not a new training campaign.

tasks.name: W10D2: finish harness interface and example report
tasks.acceptance: One documented command runs a benign example and returns loss components, observed uplift, forecast interval, costs and out-of-distribution flags.

tasks.name: Specify forecasting baselines and grouped holdouts
tasks.acceptance: Compare constant/mean, small-budget extrapolation, zero-shot-only, low-budget-only and combined forecasters; split complete model/curriculum trajectories, not budget points or rollout seeds.

tasks.name: W9D1: fit forecasters and save held-out predictions
tasks.acceptance: Fit using development-only high-budget targets from two models plus their zero-shot/b/4b inputs; use at most two prespecified features. Save predictions for the third model and unseen cases before reading held-out high-budget outcomes.

tasks.name: W9D3-4: score high-budget forecasts and uncertainty
tasks.acceptance: Report MAE/RMSE of uplift, interval coverage and rank errors versus baselines; uncertainty grouped by independent worlds/studies; three models do not justify broad model-family generalization.

tasks.name: W9D4: mechanism-shift, study and signature ablations
tasks.acceptance: Held-out mechanism/study results and leave-model-out diagnostics retained, including failure to forecast; remove each stress signature component; bounded claim about benign biological reasoning.

tasks.name: W9D5: resource-capability frontier and decision linkage
tasks.acceptance: Separate training spend from inference spend; show capability/quality versus each; illustrate how uncertain forecasting informs evaluation allocation without claiming measured CBRN risk.

tasks.name: W9D5: independent result and leakage review
tasks.acceptance: Reviewer checks token accounting, grouped splits, baseline identity, unsupported claims and figure provenance; correctness bugs use buffer, exploratory reruns do not delay the freeze.

tasks.name: Create paper skeleton and required-output checklist
tasks.acceptance: One paper narrative: forecast post-training scientific reasoning uplift, with the emergency scientist as applied case. Each mandatory SynX/grant output has an evidence file and responsible owner.

tasks.name: Map closest prior work and sharpen novelty
tasks.acceptance: Compare capability forecasting, scaling/extrapolation, agentic science, controlled counterfactual benchmarks and molecular agents; identify falsifiable distinction before new policy engineering.

tasks.name: Draft introduction, task definitions and evaluation plan
tasks.acceptance: Problem, hypotheses, inference/training budget distinction and endpoint limits written; figures have planned data sources and no fabricated results.

tasks.name: Draft methods and prototype figure
tasks.acceptance: Agent state, benchmark worlds, loss components, splits and baselines are described well enough to reproduce; architecture figure connects both testbeds without conflating their evidence.

tasks.name: Build artifact skeleton and results table templates
tasks.acceptance: Environment lock, data licensing, source manifest and clean-run entry point exist; all anticipated figure/table columns and independent unit definitions are specified.

tasks.name: Write SynX results and pre-London presentation outline
tasks.acceptance: Historical/two-family results and platform improvement written; no placeholder science claims; one-slide London feedback questions and experimental caveats included.
tasks.note: Talk outline and results draft are due W6D5; light narrative revisions continue during London, with final case text by W7D5.

tasks.name: London: collect expert feedback and case-study narrative
tasks.acceptance: Expert review facts and quotations are attributable and cleared for publication where needed; technical disagreements and constraints retained.

tasks.name: W9: write safety results and final figure captions
tasks.acceptance: Low-budget placeholders replaced only after corresponding high-budget scoring; captions state independent units, uncertainty, costs, failed forecasts and boundary of safety inference.
tasks.note: Starts with table scaffolding at W9D2; final values depend on FCAST-03/FCAST-04 by W9D4.

tasks.name: W10D1-2: close full paper and permitted artifact
tasks.acceptance: All sections, references, limitations, required-output checklist, commands and permitted data are complete; choose actual venue/template/deadline after checking current calls.

tasks.name: W10D3: expert review and first full rehearsal
tasks.acceptance: Askar/one external reviewer tests the claim chain and demo; full talk fits the actual allotted presentation time; any lab obligation still missing is explicitly identified.

tasks.name: W10D4: final deck, demo recording and offline backup
tasks.acceptance: Second rehearsal succeeds without live API/network; numbers match frozen paper; artifact opens from clean environment; presentation and demo backups available.

tasks.name: W10D5: final presentation and deliverable handoff
tasks.artifact: presentation + paper + reproducible artifact + SynX handoff
tasks.acceptance: Deliver talk, submission-ready manuscript, harness, benchmark manifests and seven mandatory SynX outputs; log publication status as submitted/ready only if actually true.

assumptions: Week 1 began September 28. London is the November 8 week; W7 workdays are November 9-13. Exact itinerary and final talk day are unconfirmed.
Rebaselined from October 14 (W3D3) and updated October 19 (W4D1); elapsed weeks are not marked complete without evidence.

Task ids carry their stream: GATE decisions and access, COSCI the emergency co-scientist, MOL macrocycle design and platform, LAB the SynX experiment and London, SAFE the safety benchmark, TRAIN the training harness, FCAST forecasting, PAPER the write-up.

Four tasks are marked Complete and each names a committed artifact; COSCI-07 is Prepared pending sign-off and MOL-01 is Blocked on the SynX export. Everything else is planned, including the lab slot and model access.
One principal researcher; SynX staff execute the laboratory work.
Main Tinker implementation is W8-W10; prerequisites are prepared W1-W6.
effort_definition: Remaining hands-on hours, spread uniformly across each task window; tasks marked Complete are excluded. Replace with real estimates after access/throughput review. Travel and SynX staff hours are excluded.
